import re
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from buvis.pybase.filesystem.atomic_write import atomic_write_text

from sysup.step_result import StepResult

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping

__all__ = ["PipxPython"]

_DEFAULT_CONFIG = "~/.config/mise/config.toml"
_PIN = re.compile(r'^"(pipx:[^"]+)" = .*--managed-python --python (\d+\.\d+)', re.MULTILINE)
_MINOR = re.compile(r"^(\d+\.\d+)")


def _set_pin(path: Path, tool: str, version: str) -> None:
    pattern = re.compile(rf'^("{re.escape(tool)}" = .*--managed-python --python )\d+\.\d+', re.MULTILINE)
    atomic_write_text(path, pattern.sub(rf"\g<1>{version}", path.read_text(), count=1))


class PipxPython:
    """Move mise pipx tools pinned to uv-managed python onto the global mise python minor.

    Only entries whose ``uvx_args`` carry ``--managed-python --python X.Y`` are
    touched. Each stale pin is rewritten in the mise config and the tool is
    reinstalled; a tool that fails to install on the new minor is reverted to
    its old pin and reinstalled there, so one bad wheel never leaves it broken.
    """

    @property
    def inputs(self: PipxPython) -> Mapping[str, object]:
        return {"config": _DEFAULT_CONFIG}

    def run(self: PipxPython, **kwargs: object) -> Iterator[StepResult]:
        mise, uv = shutil.which("mise"), shutil.which("uv")
        if mise is None or uv is None:
            yield StepResult("pipx python", success=False, message="mise or uv not found, skipping")
            return

        path = Path(str(kwargs.get("config", _DEFAULT_CONFIG))).expanduser()
        if not path.is_file():
            yield StepResult("pipx python", success=False, message=f"{path} not found, skipping")
            return

        target = self._global_minor(mise)
        if target is None:
            yield StepResult("pipx python", success=False, message="no global mise python version, skipping")
            return

        stale = [(m.group(1), m.group(2)) for m in _PIN.finditer(path.read_text()) if m.group(2) != target]
        if not stale:
            yield StepResult("pipx python", success=True, message=f"all pinned pipx tools on python {target}")
            return

        install = subprocess.run([uv, "python", "install", target], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
        if install.returncode != 0:
            message = install.stderr.strip() or "unknown error"
            yield StepResult("pipx python", success=False, message=f"uv python install {target} failed: {message}")
            return

        for tool, old in stale:
            yield self._move(mise, path, tool, old, target)

    def _global_minor(self: PipxPython, mise: str) -> str | None:
        # Run from $HOME so a project-local python pin can't redefine the target.
        result = subprocess.run(
            [mise, "current", "python"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=False,
            cwd=Path.home(),
        )
        match = _MINOR.match(result.stdout.strip()) if result.returncode == 0 else None
        return match.group(1) if match else None

    def _move(self: PipxPython, mise: str, path: Path, tool: str, old: str, target: str) -> StepResult:
        label = f"{tool} (python {old} -> {target})"
        _set_pin(path, tool, target)
        result = subprocess.run([mise, "install", "-f", tool], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
        if result.returncode == 0:
            return StepResult(label, success=True)

        message = result.stderr.strip() or "unknown error"
        _set_pin(path, tool, old)
        restore = subprocess.run([mise, "install", "-f", tool], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
        state = f"kept on python {old}" if restore.returncode == 0 else f"reinstall on python {old} also failed"
        return StepResult(label, success=False, message=f"{state}: {message}")

    marks a key the config validator treats as required on an enabled item.
    ``expires_at`` returns an aware :class:`datetime.datetime` when the expiry is
    known, or a :class:`str` naming why it is unknown. A probe may raise
    :class:`buvis.pybase.result.FatalError` for an unrecoverable precondition;
    any other exception is caught by the runner and reported as unknown.
    """

    @property
    def inputs(self: ExpiryCapability) -> Mapping[str, object]: ...

    def expires_at(self: ExpiryCapability, **kwargs: object) -> datetime | str: ...

# Bundled default sysup configuration.
#
# Reproduces the behaviour of the former `sysup mac` and `sysup wsl`
# subcommands, host-selected via each entry's `when`. It is the lowest-priority
# layer: any `buvis-sysup.yaml` (or its machine-local `.local.yaml` twin) in the
# config stack deep-merges on top by key, so a machine can add, reorder, or
# disable (`enabled: false`) an entry without redefining this base.

commands:
  # --- macOS (former `sysup mac`) -----------------------------------------
  brew:
    order: 10
    when: { os: darwin, check: brew }
    sudo: true
    steps:
      - [brew, update]
      - [brew, upgrade]
      - [brew, cleanup]

  npm-check:
    order: 20
    when: { os: darwin, check: npm-check }
    interactive: true
    steps:
      - [npm-check, -gu]

  python-packages:
    order: 30
    when: { os: darwin }
    use: pip-outdated

  uv:
    order: 40
    when: { os: darwin, check: uv }
    steps:
      - [uv, python, upgrade]
      - [uv, tool, upgrade, --all]

  helm:
    order: 50
    when: { os: darwin, check: helm }
    use: helm-repo-update

  # `mise upgrade` deletes replaced tool-version dirs that the inherited PATH
  # still points at, so it must run after every other tool lookup — hence the
  # highest `order` among the macOS entries.
  mise:
    order: 60
    when: { os: darwin, check: mise }
    steps:
      - [mise, self-update, --yes]
      - [mise, upgrade]

  # Moves mise pipx tools pinned with `--managed-python --python X.Y` onto the
  # global mise python minor. After `mise upgrade` so it sees the new global
  # python; before nvim so pynvim is settled when Mason spawns nvim.
  pipx-python:
    order: 65
    when: { os: darwin, check: mise }
    use: pipx-python

  # --- Cross-platform (former standalone `sysup nvim`) --------------------
  # The old `sysup nvim` subcommand had no platform guard — it ran wherever
  # nvim resolved. `order: 70` keeps it after `mise upgrade` (and after every
  # macOS tool lookup), so a version-manager churn that replaces the nvim
  # binary happens before the headless Mason update spawns it.
  nvim:
    order: 70
    when: { check: nvim }
    use: nvim-mason

  # --- WSL / Linux (former `sysup wsl`) -----------------------------------
  apt:
    order: 10
    when: { os: linux, check: apt }
    steps:
      - [sudo, apt, update]
      - [sudo, apt, upgrade, -y]
      - [sudo, apt, autoremove, -y]

  snap:
    order: 20
    when: { os: linux, check: snap }
    steps:
      - [sudo, snap, refresh]

# Session-level capabilities that run before any command. sudo priming caches
# credentials up front so brew casks don't prompt mid-run (former mac behaviour).
prime:
  - sudo-prime

# Expiring credentials checked before every ordinary run (PRD 00096). gh-agent
# is a disabled template: in buvis-sysup.local.yaml set `with.probe` to a
# `gh api` path that needs private-repository access (for example
# repos/<owner>/<private-repo>) and `enabled: true`. The other fields merge in.
expiry:
  gh-agent:
    enabled: false
    use: gh-token-expiry
    with:
      config_dir: ~/.config/gh-agent
    warn_days: 30
    refresh:
      instructions: |
        1. Open https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new
        2. Token name: gh-agent. Resource owner: buvis. Expiration: 1 year.
        3. Repository access: All repositories.
        4. Permissions: Pull requests (read and write), Issues (read and write),
           Actions (read), Commit statuses (read), Contents (read), Metadata (read).
        5. Generate the token, copy it, and paste it at the prompt below.
      commands:
        - argv: [gh, auth, login, --hostname, github.com, --with-token, --insecure-storage]
          env: { GH_CONFIG_DIR: ~/.config/gh-agent }
          stdin: secret

# Codex Implementor Mechanics

Extracted verbatim from SKILL.md step 3 (2026-08-09; situational: consulted only
when the codex rung interception can fire). SKILL.md § Codex rung interception
decides WHETHER codex dispatches; this file owns HOW — the batch health probe,
the dispatch checklist, and the hook-gate notice. Read it in full before the
first codex probe or dispatch of a batch.

## Codex rung interception

Moved verbatim out of SKILL.md step 3 (PRD 00119-v2). SKILL.md keeps the
one-line rule and the pointer; the six fences live here.

> **Codex rung interception.** After SKILL.md step 3's deterministic routing table yields its verdict, when ALL
> of the following hold, dispatch **codex** instead of the Claude implementor the
> table named:
>
> 1. the table's verdict is "Claude at the task's tier" or "Claude at the task's
>    ORIGINAL tier" (i.e. rows 3, 4, 6, or 7 fired — never rows 1, 2, or 5), and
> 2. `codex_eligible(task)` per `model-ladder.md § Codex rung`, and
> 3. `_WORK_CODEX_RUNG != "off"`, and
> 4. `_AUTOPILOT_ESCALATION != "legacy"`, and
> 5. the batch codex health probe verdict is `"healthy"`, and
> 6. the task's own TERMINAL attempt (the last entry in `task.attempts`, if any)
>    was not itself codex.
>
> The interception never fires for a `fable` task (that override outranks the
> whole table), never for a UI task, and never for `opus` tier — fence 2 and the
> `fable` rule already exclude all three. It also never re-fires on a task whose
> terminal attempt was codex: per `run-autopilot/references/phase-review.md`
> ("terminal attempt with `implementor: codex` -> re-dispatch Claude at the
> task's same tier"), a review-flagged codex rework escalates to Claude at the
> task's own tier, never back to codex.

**Why fence 4 is required, not optional.** `model-ladder.md` promises that under `_AUTOPILOT_ESCALATION=legacy` the escalation machinery is byte-identical to pre-00065. The legacy branch of step 5.5 has no codex arm, so letting the interception fire under `legacy` would both falsify that promise and send a failing codex attempt into "escalate to the user" — in a headless loop, a stall with no defined `site:`, i.e. a new halt class. Gating the interception is cheaper than adding a codex carve-out to the legacy branch.

**Routing row 3 (qwen breaker tripped) IS codex-eligible — stated intent.** The qwen capability breaker fences *qwen*, not the whole non-Claude family: it latches on two consecutive qwen test-gate failures, which is evidence about the local model, not about codex. A breakered batch is when the rung absorbs the most traffic.

## Codex batch health probe

Same placement and the same batch scope as the qwen preflight — one probe
decides the codex rung for every task in the batch:

```
state.codex_probe = {
  "batch_id":   "<state.batch.id, or \"no-batch\">",
  "verdict":    "healthy" | "unhealthy",
  "backend":    "codex" | "copilot",
  "detail":     "<one-line cause on unhealthy, else null>",
  "checked_at": "<ISO 8601>"
}
```

**Batch-scope check, before any read or write** — the same lazy-reset idiom
`qwen_breaker` already uses: compute the effective batch id
`(state.batch.id // "no-batch")` and compare it to `codex_probe.batch_id`.
Mismatch or field absent → re-probe and overwrite the slice. Match → reuse the
cached verdict, never re-probe.

**Doctor-first.** Once the batch-scope check above says a re-probe is needed,
run the hook doctor before the live probe — a foreground Bash local file scan,
no dispatch:

```
python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-codex/scripts/codex_hook_doctor.py check
```

Exit 1 (a broken target exists): write `codex_probe.verdict: "unhealthy"`,
`detail: "hook_doctor: <the first broken TSV line>"`, `hook_doctor: "<the
doctor's own summary line>"`, and `backend` as resolved by `command -v
codex` — then skip the live probe below entirely (no codex dispatch this
batch, infra semantics, no escalation stamp).

Exit 2 (the doctor itself could not run): on this path the doctor emits no
per-target TSV line and no summary line — only a single `error: <reason>`
line to stderr. Write `codex_probe.verdict: "unhealthy"`,
`detail: "hook_doctor: <the doctor's stderr error line>"`,
`hook_doctor: "doctor error: <config path>"`, and `backend` as resolved by
`command -v codex` — then skip the live probe below entirely (no codex
dispatch this batch, infra semantics, no escalation stamp). The causes: the
config is missing, unreadable, not JSON, or has no `hooks` object; an event
entry is malformed; a command does not tokenize; the plugin manifest has no
`aegis@buvis-plugins` entry; a target I/O call failed. The stderr line names
which.

Exit 0 or 3: run the live probe unchanged below, and add
`hook_doctor: "ok"` (exit 0) or `hook_doctor: "stale: <basenames>"` (exit 3,
the stale/no_canonical targets' basenames) to the slice — a stale hook copy
does not gate the rung by itself; the live probe below still decides
`"healthy"`/`"unhealthy"`. **A batch never runs `repair`:** the unattended
write fence denies writes under `~/.codex`, and `repair` is the operator's
explicit command, never something a batch invokes on its own.

**The probe must EXERCISE TOOL USE, not just completion.** Dispatch it exactly
like a real implementor run:

```
Bash (run_in_background: true):
  ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-codex/scripts/codex-run.sh -a \
    -f <abs tmp prompt file> -o <abs tmp out file>
then: TaskOutput(task_id, block=true, timeout=300000)
```

The probe writes only to `docs/dev/tmp/`, inside the repo's normal
workspace. Do not widen the sandbox with `-d`.

Prompt file contents: the TOOL-GATE NOTICE block from § Hook interaction
verbatim, followed by these three lines with `<nonce>` substituted (a fresh
per-probe value, e.g. `<batch_id>-<uuid4>`):

```
Create the file docs/dev/tmp/codex-probe-<nonce>.txt containing exactly: <nonce>
Then run: git status --porcelain docs/dev/tmp/codex-probe-<nonce>.txt
Reply with the single word: done
```

The notice is required for the same reason every real dispatch carries it: the
probe performs exactly the two actions the gate intercepts (first `Write` to a
path, first `Bash` of the session).

Verdict is `"healthy"` iff ALL of: the helper exited 0, the `-o` file is
non-empty, AND `docs/dev/tmp/codex-probe-<nonce>.txt` exists on disk with
content equal to `<nonce>`. Delete the file after the verdict is written.
**The nonce is load-bearing:** a fixed filename would still be on disk from a
previous batch (`docs/dev/tmp/` is GC'd only at 7 days), so a fully
hook-blocked run — exit 0, a non-empty `-o` explaining the deny, and last
batch's leftover file — would satisfy every condition and report `healthy`.

**Why a tool-less probe is rejected.** A prompt like "reply with the word ok"
invokes zero tools, so it returns `"healthy"` in exactly the state that kills a
real run. Measured, not hypothetical: a codex reviewer in this repo died on
`Command blocked by PreToolUse hook: [Fact-Forcing Gate]`, retried until its
run was exhausted, and emitted no findings — while a completion probe would
have reported perfect health. Same trap the qwen stack taught one layer up.

**Watchdog and cleanup (no new halt class).** Background-dispatched with a
`TaskOutput` deadline like every other helper-script call — never a bare
foreground CLI call, the canonical way to hang an unattended session. A timeout
return is verdict `"unhealthy"`, `detail: "probe_timeout"`, followed by
`TaskStop` on the probe task so it cannot outlive the decision. **300s, not
120s:** the probe must survive two one-shot gate denials (restate facts, retry)
plus a final reply — five-plus model round trips, against the qwen preflight's
~2 min budget for a single 1-token completion. A `probe_timeout` is fail-safe
(rung off, batch continues, no halt) but indistinguishable from real
ill-health, so the batch-report probe-verdict line is the signal to re-tune it.

**Backend check.** `codex-run.sh` silently falls back to `copilot` when `codex`
is not on PATH, and a premium Copilot model once burned 25% of monthly Copilot
quota in one run — the same quota the UI reviewer lens runs on. A
cost-reduction rung that silently drains the UI reviewer inverts its own
premise. Record the resolved backend (`command -v codex`) in
`state.codex_probe.backend`; `backend == "copilot"` is verdict `"unhealthy"`,
`detail: "copilot_fallback_not_authorized_for_implementor"`.

**No exit-4 clause.** `codex-run.sh` has no exit 4 and writes no
`codex-review-last.jsonl` — both belong to
`run-autopilot/scripts/codex_review_run.py`, a wrapper the implementor path
does not use. The real empty-output signal for this helper is its own "codex
exited 0 but wrote no output" warning, already covered by the non-empty `-o`
condition.

**On `"unhealthy"`** — every codex interception is skipped for the rest of the
batch; affected tasks take the Claude implementor the table already named, with
**no** escalation stamp (infra semantics).

## Codex dispatch

Reuses `use-codex/references/dispatch-contract.md`, whose § Implementor-mode
divergence records the three rules this path departs from (exit-code trust,
contract-level retry, the `-a` grant) — that file wins on disagreement, so read
the departures there, not here:

- **No-edit probe: before-capture.** Immediately before this background Bash
  dispatch, capture porcelain for the task's own file slice — never the whole
  worktree, so a concurrent user edit elsewhere cannot mask this arm:
  `git --git-dir=<bare-git-dir> --work-tree=<work-tree> status --porcelain -- <file slice>`;
- background Bash, never Agent-wrapped (era invariant: a subagent that shells
  out to a CLI hangs);
- `-f <prompt file>` and `-o <output file>`, absolute paths. The prompt file
  is step 3's render, `docs/dev/tmp/dispatch-ivan-<task-id>.txt` (opened with
  the two telemetry flags), with § Hook interaction's TOOL-GATE NOTICE appended
  in-session — Read the rendered file, then append with the Edit tool; a shell
  redirect into `docs/dev/project-management/` is blocked — so the dispatch's row and id are the
  render's;
- `TaskOutput(task_id, block=true, timeout=600000)` as the watchdog;
- **No-edit probe: after-capture.** Immediately after `TaskOutput` returns,
  before step 4 hands off, capture porcelain again with the same command and
  file slice. Latch the before/after comparison as `codex_no_edit` in the
  attempt record — step 5.5 reads only this latched flag and never re-runs
  `git status`. A non-zero exit on either capture is INDETERMINATE, not "no
  change": do not latch `codex_no_edit`; record the exit code in
  `codex_no_edit_probe_exit` instead and continue through the capability path
  normally;
- close the dispatch row when `TaskOutput` returns —
  `record_dispatch.py end <id> --outcome ok`, `error` on a non-zero exit,
  `lost` when the `-o` file is missing or empty, `timeout` after the second
  deadline (`references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Dispatch telemetry). The
  Claude fallback that re-sends that file keeps the id and closes it again
  when it returns; a continuation brief re-rendered through gate-failure.md
  § Retry render opens its own row through the render's flags;
- completion judged by the `-o` file plus the step-5.5 test gate — **never by
  exit code alone**;
- **edit-enabled sandbox: `-a` (`--sandbox workspace-write`), never `-y`.**
  `-y` maps to `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, i.e. no sandbox at
  all; granting that to an unattended autonomous implementor is unbounded write
  access for no added capability, and the dispatch contract requires an
  explicit calling-skill grant before any unattended high-impact flag. **This
  bullet is that grant, and it covers `-a` at this rung only** — never `-y`,
  and never a reviewer dispatch.
- Do not add a separate `-d` grant for `docs/dev/project-management/`; it
  is a tracked directory inside the repo workspace.
- **On a `TaskOutput` timeout, kill before falling back.** `TaskStop` the codex
  background task and verify it is gone BEFORE dispatching the Claude
  fallback, then capture `git status --porcelain`. An orphaned
  `--sandbox workspace-write` codex keeps write access to the very files the
  Claude implementor is about to edit; without the kill, its late writes either
  get swept into that commit or land as unexplained foreign paths.
- **Hook-coverage delta**: this dispatch runs under a weaker `Bash`-hook set
  than a Claude implementor — see `model-ladder.md` § Codex rung ("Hook
  coverage").

## Hook interaction

Codex's tool calls are gated by this host's own PreToolUse hooks, and this is
the single largest execution risk in the rung: `~/.codex/hooks.json` registers
PreToolUse hooks on codex's `Edit|Write|MultiEdit` and `Bash` matchers; the
fact-forcing gate denies the FIRST `Edit`/`Write` to each distinct `file_path`
and the FIRST `Bash` command of a session, and its deny text tells the agent to
use Grep/Glob — tools codex does not have and which do not exist in this build
at all. Observed consequence: a codex design reviewer burned its entire run
retrying blocked commands and returned nothing.

The gate is one-shot per path, so a run that understands it can proceed. Every
codex implementor prompt therefore ends with this block:

import subprocess

from sysup.capabilities.pipx_python import PipxPython

CONFIG = """[tools]
"pipx:gita" = { version = "latest", uvx_args = "--managed-python --python 3.13" }
"pipx:beets" = { version = "latest", extras = "discogs", uvx_args = "--managed-python --python 3.13" }
"pipx:ruff" = { version = "latest", uvx_args = "--managed-python --python 3.14" }
"pipx:plain" = "latest"
"pipx:legacy" = { version = "latest", uvx_args = "--python 3.12" }
python = "3.14.6"
"""


class TestPipxPython:
    @staticmethod
    def _fake_run(mocker, *, current: str = "3.14.6\n", fail: frozenset[str] = frozenset()):
        """Fake subprocess.run; ``fail`` holds tools whose first reinstall fails."""
        pending = set(fail)

        def run(argv: list[str], **_: object) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
            if argv[1:] == ["current", "python"]:
                return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, stdout=current, stderr="")
            if argv[1:3] == ["install", "-f"] and argv[3] in pending:
                pending.discard(argv[3])
                return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 1, stdout="", stderr="no wheel for 3.14")
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, stdout="", stderr="")

        mocker.patch("sysup.capabilities.pipx_python.shutil.which", side_effect=lambda name: f"/bin/{name}")
        return mocker.patch("sysup.capabilities.pipx_python.subprocess.run", side_effect=run)

    def test_moves_stale_pins_to_global_minor_and_reinstalls(self, mocker, tmp_path) -> None:
        config = tmp_path / "config.toml"
        config.write_text(CONFIG)
        mock_run = self._fake_run(mocker)

        steps = list(PipxPython().run(config=str(config)))

        assert [s.success for s in steps] == [True, True]
        assert [s.label for s in steps] == [
            "pipx:gita (python 3.13 -> 3.14)",
            "pipx:beets (python 3.13 -> 3.14)",
        ]
        text = config.read_text()
        assert text.count("--managed-python --python 3.14") == 3
        assert "--managed-python --python 3.13" not in text
        calls = [c.args[0] for c in mock_run.call_args_list]
        assert ["/bin/uv", "python", "install", "3.14"] in calls
        assert ["/bin/mise", "install", "-f", "pipx:gita"] in calls

    def test_leaves_unmanaged_and_current_entries_untouched(self, mocker, tmp_path) -> None:
        config = tmp_path / "config.toml"
        config.write_text(CONFIG)
        mock_run = self._fake_run(mocker)

        list(PipxPython().run(config=str(config)))

        text = config.read_text()
        assert '"pipx:legacy" = { version = "latest", uvx_args = "--python 3.12" }' in text
        assert '"pipx:plain" = "latest"' in text
        reinstalled = [c.args[0][3] for c in mock_run.call_args_list if c.args[0][1:3] == ["install", "-f"]]
        assert "pipx:ruff" not in reinstalled
        assert "pipx:legacy" not in reinstalled

    def test_reverts_pin_when_tool_fails_on_new_minor(self, mocker, tmp_path) -> None:
        config = tmp_path / "config.toml"
        config.write_text(CONFIG)
        mock_run = self._fake_run(mocker, fail=frozenset({"pipx:beets"}))

        steps = list(PipxPython().run(config=str(config)))

        beets = next(s for s in steps if s.label.startswith("pipx:beets"))
        assert beets.success is False
        assert "kept on python 3.13" in beets.message
        assert "no wheel for 3.14" in beets.message
        beets_line = next(line for line in config.read_text().splitlines() if line.startswith('"pipx:beets"'))
        assert beets_line.endswith('uvx_args = "--managed-python --python 3.13" }')
        beets_install = ["/bin/mise", "install", "-f", "pipx:beets"]
        assert [c.args[0] for c in mock_run.call_args_list].count(beets_install) == 2

    def test_all_current_is_a_noop(self, mocker, tmp_path) -> None:
        config = tmp_path / "config.toml"
        config.write_text(CONFIG.replace("--python 3.13", "--python 3.14"))
        mock_run = self._fake_run(mocker)

        steps = list(PipxPython().run(config=str(config)))

        assert steps[0].success is True
        assert "on python 3.14" in steps[0].message
        assert all(c.args[0][1] != "install" for c in mock_run.call_args_list)

    def test_no_global_python_skips_without_touching_config(self, mocker, tmp_path) -> None:
        config = tmp_path / "config.toml"
        config.write_text(CONFIG)
        self._fake_run(mocker, current="")

        steps = list(PipxPython().run(config=str(config)))

        assert steps[0].success is False
        assert "no global mise python" in steps[0].message
        assert config.read_text() == CONFIG

    def test_missing_config_skips(self, mocker, tmp_path) -> None:
        self._fake_run(mocker)

        steps = list(PipxPython().run(config=str(tmp_path / "absent.toml")))

        assert steps[0].success is False
        assert "not found" in steps[0].message

import os

    if os.environ.get("BUVIS_SNAPSHOT_CANONICAL") == "1":
        return True
    return sys.platform.startswith(SNAPSHOT_CANONICAL_PLATFORM) and sys.version_info[:2] == SNAPSHOT_CANONICAL_PYTHON


def pytest_collection_modifyitems(config: pytest.Config, items: list[pytest.Item]) -> None:
    """Auto-apply tool/lib markers by path and gate snapshot tests to canonical env."""
    canonical = _snapshot_env_is_canonical()
    skip_snapshot = pytest.mark.skip(
        reason=(
            f"snapshot baselines are canonical on {SNAPSHOT_CANONICAL_PLATFORM} + "
            f"Python {SNAPSHOT_CANONICAL_PYTHON[0]}.{SNAPSHOT_CANONICAL_PYTHON[1]}; "
            "run the update-snapshots workflow to regenerate"
        ),
    )
    for item in items:
        rel = item.path.as_posix()
        if "/tests/tools/" in rel:
            parts = rel.split("/tests/tools/")[1].split("/")
            if parts:
                tool_name = parts[0]
                item.add_marker(getattr(pytest.mark, tool_name))
        elif "/tests/lib/" in rel:
            item.add_marker(pytest.mark.lib)

        if not canonical and "snapshot" in item.keywords:

## Loop-mode stall procedure (PRD 00017)

The uniform "a single PRD may stall; the batch never stops to ask a question"
procedure. Every loop-mode failure site references THIS section instead of
pausing. Interactive (non-loop) sites keep their PAUSE semantics.

Run `autopilot stall --prd <filename> --site <slug> --detail <one-line detail>`
(one call). It stamps a durable intent (`state.stall_op`), performs the
verified `wip/`→`hold/` move, appends an op_id-deduped deferred record, and
closes with the single-commit reset + `parks_consecutive` rule — recoverable
on retry from a kill at any internal boundary. See `cli/records.py`'s
`do_stall` docstring for the full contract. **The deferred record is
distinct from `state.stall_reason`** — that field is the wrapper's replan
signal (`subagent_prompt_overrun`, branch 2 of the Session Loop decision
table); `do_stall` never writes it (its own per-PRD reset clears it instead).

| Exit code | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | stalled | print the STALLED banner, continue the batch |
| 4 | move failed | PAUSE per the mv-verify invariant (`site: "mv_verify"`) |

# sysup uv-tool-python: design draft

Source PRD: `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/00105-sysup-uv-tool-python-pin-v1.md`. This draft refines implementation contracts; the PRD and its acceptance criteria remain unchanged.

## Architecture fit

Add one built-in sysup capability beside `PipxPython`, using the existing `Capability` protocol and `StepResult` generator seam. Configuration selects it through `CAPABILITIES`; `Runner._run_use` already handles dry runs, result stamping, run logs, and controlled exception reporting. CLI, attention, and persistence behavior need no new implementation.

The root `AGENTS.md` and `docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md` govern placement and interface separation. The older `docs/dev/context/project-capsule.md` supplies background only. No nested `AGENTS.md` exists in this checkout; the optional cartographer atlas is absent. Reuse the sibling's orchestration pattern without importing its private helpers or refactoring it.

## Module placement

| Path | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/tools/sysup/capabilities/uv_tool_python.py` | New capability and its private discovery/version helpers. |
| `src/tools/sysup/capabilities/__init__.py` | Import `UvToolPython`; register its instance under `uv-tool-python`. |
| `src/tools/sysup/default.yaml` | Add the independent order-35 entry before the existing order-40 uv entry. |
| `tests/tools/sysup/test_uv_tool_python.py` | New class-based tests with temporary receipt trees and fake subprocess calls. |
| `tests/tools/sysup/test_default_config.py` | Update the exact Darwin plan and assert entry order, guard, use name, and unchanged uv steps. |
| `docs/source/tools/sysup.rst` | Describe pinning, failure recovery, and safety skips in the capabilities/configuration documentation. |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Add the PRD's sysup item under `[Unreleased] / Added`. |

`tests/tools/sysup/test_invariants.py` already globs every capability module and needs no edit. No new dependency, CLI option, public library API, receipt writer, or runner behavior is needed.

## Interfaces & contracts

The new module exports exactly `__all__ = ["UvToolPython"]`. Use modern type annotations, `TYPE_CHECKING` imports for `Iterator`/`Mapping`, stdlib `tomllib`, argv subprocess calls, and no direct output or process exit.

```python
_MINOR = re.compile(r"^(\d+\.\d+)")

def _tool_dir(uv: str) -> Path: ...
def _global_minor(mise: str) -> str | None: ...
def _pinned_minor(receipt_path: Path) -> str | None: ...

class UvToolPython:
    @property
    def inputs(self: UvToolPython) -> Mapping[str, object]: ...

    def run(self: UvToolPython, **kwargs: object) -> Iterator[StepResult]: ...

    def _move(
        self: UvToolPython, uv: str, tool: str, old: str | None, target: str
    ) -> StepResult: ...
```

`inputs` returns `{}`: this PRD introduces no `with:` keys. `run` resolves `uv` and `mise` using `shutil.which` on each invocation. Missing either yields exactly one `StepResult("uv tool python", success=False, message="uv or mise not found, skipping")` and stops. `_global_minor` runs `[mise, "current", "python"]` with `cwd=Path.home()`, `capture_output=True`, `text=True`, `check=False`; a nonzero result or unmatched stripped stdout returns `None`. That produces `success=False`, message `no global mise python version, skipping`, and no install command.

`_tool_dir` runs `[uv, "tool", "dir"]` with captured text and `check=False`. Use a successful nonempty stripped path; otherwise use nonempty `$XDG_DATA_HOME/uv/tools`, otherwise `Path.home() / ".local/share/uv/tools"`. Do not create the directory. A missing root is empty; a root that exists but cannot be listed yields a failed discovery result, not a false no-tools success. Enumerate sorted immediate subdirectories only; ignore files and dot-prefixed metadata directories. Resolve receipt names from directory names without invoking a shell.

`_pinned_minor` reads `uv-receipt.toml` with `tomllib`, requires a `[tool]` table, and returns the leading `X.Y` from a supported numeric version string. An absent `python` key alone returns `None`. Compare minor tuples `(int(major), int(minor))`, never strings: move an absent pin or one below the target; leave equal and newer pins untouched. This follows the PRD's “below the global” predicate rather than copying the sibling's `!=` predicate, which could downgrade a deliberate newer pin.

Safety preflight is part of `_pinned_minor`, before any reinstall. A bare-name reinstall is supported only for a receipt whose original request is that same normalized package name with no customization: `requirements` is exactly `[tool_name]` in the legacy string form or `[{"name": tool_name}]` in uv's structured form; normalize names by lowercasing and collapsing `[-_.]+` to `-`. Explicitly empty `extras` and empty `specifier` in that single structured requirement are also harmless. `constraints`, `overrides`, `excludes`, and `build-constraint-dependencies` must be absent or empty; `options` must be absent or `{}`. Allow uv-owned `entrypoints` metadata but reject an entrypoint with a nonempty `from` naming a different package. Unknown substantive keys in `[tool]` or the requirement object are unsupported. These checks ensure the PRD's bare `<tool>` argv cannot discard an original source, extras, dependency injection, index, constraint, or resolver option.

Missing/malformed receipts, a missing requirements identity, unsupported customizations, and a present `python` that is not a numeric version are distinguishable failures, never silently treated as an unpinned plain package. Catch `OSError`, `tomllib.TOMLDecodeError`, and validation `ValueError` per tool, yield `StepResult(tool, success=False, message="<reason>, skipping")`, and continue other tools. Numeric selectors match `\d+\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?` with an optional prerelease suffix; selectors such as `pypy@3.10`, `cpython@3.14`, paths, executable names, ranges, and free-threaded `3.14t` remain untouched with an explicit unsupported-selector failure. Do not add selector resolution or a general receipt-to-argv translator in this PRD.

This is a deliberate safety refinement of the PRD's malformed-receipt fallback: without readable installation intent, a bare package reinstall cannot guarantee recovery. It changes no acceptance criterion or named scenario; it reports the unsupported case visibly instead of claiming that parsing failure proves an ordinary unpinned install.

If the root has no candidate tools, yield exactly one successful result with message `no uv tools installed`. If all safely read pins equal the target, yield exactly one successful result with message `all uv tools on python <target>`. If there are only equal/newer pins and at least one newer pin, use the truthful message `all uv tools pinned to python <target> or newer`. Never emit an all-current success when any receipt was skipped with failure. When there are eligible moves, run `[uv, "python", "install", target]` once before the first move. If it fails, yield one failed result containing `uv python install <target> failed: <stderr-or-unknown error>` and stop without tool installs.

`_move` returns one `StepResult` labelled `<tool> (python <old-or-unpinned> -> <target>)`. Its initial argv is exactly `[uv, "tool", "install", "--python", target, "--force", tool]`. On exit zero, return success. On nonzero exit or `OSError`, attempt rollback for that tool: `[uv, "tool", "install", "--python", old, "--force", tool]` when previously pinned, or `[uv, "tool", "install", "--force", tool]` when previously unpinned. All installs capture text and use `check=False`. Do not edit receipts directly; uv owns its environment and receipt writes. Continue processing later tools after either outcome.

Only a zero rollback exit permits `kept on python <old>` or `kept unpinned` in the failed result. A failed rollback reports `reinstall on python <old> also failed` or `unpinned reinstall also failed`, including both initial and rollback diagnostics. Never claim a working tool after failed recovery. Use `stderr.strip()` with `unknown error` fallback for nonzero commands. An `OSError` supplies its exception text. Unpinned rollback restores absence of an explicit request, not necessarily the identical historical interpreter; no stronger recovery claim is made. Recovery of exact package versions, or an environment snapshot, is outside this PRD's contract.

The registry addition is exactly `"uv-tool-python": UvToolPython()`. Preserve the registry module's current `__all__` public surface. Add this bundled command entry:

```yaml
  # Pin freestanding uv tools to the global python minor before uv tool upgrade.
  uv-tool-python:
    order: 35
    when: { os: darwin, check: uv }
    use: uv-tool-python
```

Keep `uv.order == 40` and its steps exactly `(("uv", "python", "upgrade"), ("uv", "tool", "upgrade", "--all"))`. Before implementation, recheck that premise; if it changed, stop and report as the PRD requires. No command dependency or fail-fast policy is added: this capability reports failed tools while the existing runner continues its normal plan.

## Data flow

1. The existing config loader merges defaults and host overrides; its applicable-command sorter places `uv-tool-python` between `python-packages` and `uv` on Darwin.
2. The runner selects the registered capability; dry run reports it without calling `run`.
3. The capability resolves binaries and the global mise minor from `$HOME`, discovers the uv tools root, and reads each receipt without writing it.
4. Receipt validation separates plain reproducible installations from unsafe or unreadable cases. Minor comparison separates eligible moves from current/newer pins.
5. One interpreter preparation precedes eligible installs. Each install produces one final result after any rollback, and later tools continue.
6. Existing runner stamping, attention, and CLI rendering consume the results. The existing order-40 uv entry subsequently performs its two upgrades.

The selected target is the global minor present at order 35. Mise's order-60 upgrade may change it later in the same run; adoption then occurs next run. Reordering mise or changing `uv python upgrade` is out of scope.

Primary uv checks: local `uv 0.13.5` help confirms install/upgrade Python flags; [uv's tool model](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/crates/uv-tool/src/tool.rs) records requirements and options, and [install logic](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/crates/uv-tool-commands/src/install.rs) constructs the request from current install inputs. Therefore bare-name install must not be assumed to replay custom receipt intent. [Storage documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/storage/#tools) confirms `uv tool dir` as the authoritative root query.

## Alternatives considered

1. **Smallest diff: transpose `PipxPython`, reinstall every discovered directory by bare package name.** This fits ordinary tools and the seven named cases, but can discard custom sources/dependencies/options, overwrite non-version selectors, downgrade newer pins, and misreport recovery. Reject that unchecked form.
2. **Chosen: the sibling pattern plus bounded receipt validation and truthful recovery.** Keep the PRD's install argv, order-35 entry, and independent capability. A small preflight skips installations whose intent cannot survive that argv. No replay framework or sibling refactor is needed. Customized receipts remain visibly unresolved rather than silently changed.
3. **Use `uv tool upgrade --python`, or implement complete receipt replay/environment backups.** Native upgrade is attractive for retaining uv-owned intent but changes the PRD's explicit reinstall/revert argv acceptance; full replay adds a second evolving receipt implementation. Both are deferred to a later requirement instead of expanding this PRD.

## Risks & edge cases

- Unknown/customized or malformed receipts stay unresolved and can still fail the subsequent batch upgrade. The design exposes this as failure; automatic repair without installation intent is not safe. This bounded coverage is explicit, while the seven PRD acceptance scenarios remain supported.
- A numeric patch pin is classified by its minor and rollback requests that prior minor, as specified by the PRD. A newer pin is preserved. A range, path, implementation-specific, or free-threaded request is not interpreted as ordinary CPython.
- A failed install can be followed by a failed rollback. Both errors must remain visible, and no successful recovery is claimed. Unpinned reinstall can select a different interpreter; this v1 restores unpinned policy rather than promising an identical environment.
- Directory fallback applies only when the root query fails or is empty. Permissions, malformed files, or unexpected schema must not become a successful empty inventory. Do not read recursively or mutate metadata entries.
- uv commands own environment locking; this capability adds no concurrent scheduler or receipt mutation. A simultaneous external install can race discovery. Avoid overwriting receipt metadata directly; a later concurrency requirement would need a separate coordinated design.
- Likely next changes are custom-receipt support through a confirmed uv-native operation, selector-aware handling, and sharing version-discovery logic with `PipxPython`. Local helpers and unchanged registry/runner seams allow these later changes without committing to a generic replay abstraction now.

## Test strategy outline

Keep all seven PRD-named tests, with real-shaped plain receipts under `tmp_path`: unpinned move, stale move, current pin no-op, failed move plus pinned/unpinned rollback, no tools, no global Python, and missing binaries. Mock every subprocess and `shutil.which`; never install an actual host tool or edit host receipts.

Add focused safety cases: numeric tuple comparison (`3.9` versus `3.14`), newer pin unchanged, patch version minor extraction, unsupported selectors unchanged, customized source/extras/with/options/constraints untouched, malformed/missing receipt fails safely, fallback root selection, interpreter-preparation failure, rollback failure including both diagnostics, `OSError` recovery, and later-tool continuation. Wiring tests assert `CAPABILITIES["uv-tool-python"]` implements `Capability`, the exact Darwin plan includes it before uv, order is 35, guard is Darwin plus `uv`, Linux excludes it, and existing uv argv remains unchanged. The invariant test's existing glob needs no extra list.

# Python Patterns

Pick a side. These are the rulings, not a tutorial.

## Idioms that earn their place

| Rule | Why |
|------|-----|
| `X \| Y`, not `Union[X, Y]` | 3.10+ runtime syntax; clearer. On 3.9 it parses only under `from __future__ import annotations` and still breaks `get_type_hints`/`isinstance` — keep `Optional`/`Union` if you support 3.9. |
| `Protocol`, not `ABC`, for duck typing | Structural typing; no inheritance you don't control. |
| `@dataclass(frozen=True)` for immutable records, plain `dataclass` only when you must mutate, `NamedTuple` for lightweight immutable rows | Pydantic only when you need validation. |
| `raise New(...) from e` | Marks the explicit cause. A bare `raise New()` still chains implicitly ("During handling..."); use `from None` to suppress. |
| `@functools.wraps` on every decorator | Without it the wrapper loses `__name__`, `__doc__`, signature. |
| `pathlib.Path`, not `os.path` | One object, no string surgery. |

## Naming (PEP 8)

`snake_case` for modules, functions, variables. `CapWords` for classes. `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for constants. Leading `_` for internal names.

**Never name a `.py` file in kebab-case.** `my-script.py` is not importable (`import my-script` is a `SyntaxError`). Kebab-case belongs only in the `pyproject.toml` distribution name and the CLI command, both of which map to a `snake_case` module.

## Traps

```python
# Mutable default argument — shared across calls
def bad(items=[]): ...
def good(items=None):
    items = [] if items is None else items

# Bare except — swallows SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt
try: ...
except Exception as e: ...        # name the exception

# __slots__ kills __dict__ and dynamic attributes — use only on fixed,
# memory-sensitive classes you won't extend.

# __double_leading is name-mangled to _Class__double_leading.
# Surprises you in subclasses, pickling, and monkey-patching.

if value is None: ...             # never == None
```

Avoid `from module import *`. Use `isinstance`, never `type(x) ==`.

## Toolchain

**black** to format, **isort** for imports, **ruff** to lint. Type annotations on every function signature — no exceptions for "obvious" returns.

## Resources and laziness

Context managers (`with`) for anything holding a resource. Generators for lazy iteration over anything you would otherwise materialize into a list.

## Security

- Read secrets with `os.environ["API_KEY"]`, never `.get()` — a missing secret must raise `KeyError` at startup, not surface as `None` at request time.
- `python-dotenv` loads a local `.env` in development only. Never commit one.
- `bandit -r src/` for static security analysis.

compatibility: "Portable standalone compatibility copy of the strunk plugin skill for agents without that plugin; Claude Code uses the namespaced plugin skill."
---

# Python Testing

TDD: write the failing test (RED), make it pass (GREEN), refactor. One behavior per test. No logic in tests. Coverage target 80%, higher on critical paths.

## Rulings

**Mocking**
- Patch where the name is *used*, not where it's defined: `@patch("myapp.service.requests")`, not `@patch("requests")`.
- `autospec=True` so the mock rejects calls the real API would reject.
- Mock at the boundary (I/O, network, clock). Never mock the thing under test.
- Async: assert with `assert_awaited_once()`, not `assert_called_once()`.

**Fixtures**
- `yield` for teardown; the line after `yield` is the cleanup.
- Default to function scope. Widen to `module`/`session` only for genuinely expensive resources.
- `autouse` hides dependencies — use sparingly; prefer explicit injection.
- `tmp_path` for temp files (auto-cleanup, `Path` API), not `tempfile`.

**Parametrize**
- `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over loops — distinct test IDs, filterable with `-k`.
- Pass `ids=[...]` when params are objects or tuples; pytest already auto-names plain str/int/bool readably.

**Config**
- One config in `pyproject.toml` (`[tool.pytest.ini_options]`), not a separate `pytest.ini`.
- `--strict-markers` so a typo'd marker fails instead of silently passing.
- Register custom markers — e.g. `slow`, `@pytest.mark.unit`, `@pytest.mark.integration` — so `--strict-markers` catches a typo.
- Coverage locally: `pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing` — the missing-line report is the point; a bare percentage is not actionable.

**Async (pytest-asyncio)**
- Default mode is `strict`: an async test with no `@pytest.mark.asyncio` is silently not collected. Set `asyncio_mode = "auto"` in `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` to drop the per-test marker.
- Use `@pytest_asyncio.fixture` for async fixtures in strict mode.

.. _tool-sysup:

sysup
=====

Configurable, dotfiles-shareable system updater. ``sysup`` runs every updater
that applies to the current host, in order. What runs is defined in
configuration, not code, so adding, removing, or reordering a simple updater is
a config edit rather than a release.

Usage
-----

.. code-block:: bash

    sysup                     # run every applicable updater, in order
    sysup --only brew,helm    # run only these entries (comma list or repeated)
    sysup --tag python        # run only entries carrying this tag
    sysup --list              # print the resolved plan for this host, run nothing
    sysup --dry-run           # show what would run without running it
    sysup status              # read unresolved attention without running updates
    sysup refresh gh-agent    # walk through renewing a tracked credential on this terminal

Applicability is decided per entry by its ``when`` guard (OS + a binary that
must exist), so there are no platform subcommands: a macOS-only entry simply
carries ``when.os: darwin`` and is skipped on other hosts.

Configuration
-------------

Updaters live in ``buvis-sysup.yaml`` in the buvis config stack
(``$BUVIS_CONFIG_DIR`` → ``~/.config/buvis`` → cwd), deep-merged over a bundled
default. The updater collection is a **flat map keyed by name**, so a machine
layer adds an entry with a new key and overrides a field of an existing entry
by that key — no list-append syntax, and every base key survives unless
explicitly disabled.

.. code-block:: yaml

    # buvis-sysup.yaml
    commands:
      brew:
        order: 10                       # entries run in ascending order
        when: { os: darwin, check: brew }
        steps:                          # run entry: argv arrays, early-abort
          - [brew, update]
          - [brew, upgrade]
          - [brew, cleanup]

      npm-check:
        order: 20
        when: { check: npm-check }
        interactive: true               # inherit stdio instead of capturing
        steps: [[npm-check, -gu]]

      python-packages:
        order: 30
        use: pip-outdated               # use entry: a named built-in capability

      nvim:
        order: 50
        when: { check: nvim }
        use: nvim-mason
        with: { timeout: 600 }          # capability inputs

    prime:                              # session capabilities run first
      - sudo-prime

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **dot**: `dot localize --shared <path>` opts a tracked file into a git clean/smudge filter instead of moving it: the file stays where it is, git stores the reserved `@HOME@` token in place of this host's home path, and each host's work tree gets its own home back on checkout. Combining `--shared` with `--to` is refused before any change. The filter itself is hidden plumbing git calls (`dot filter clean|smudge <path>`): a pure byte transform that preserves line endings, BOM and non-UTF-8 content, and refuses any file that already contains `@HOME@`.
- **sysup**: a `sudo: true` flag on an entry (or any step starting with `sudo`) primes a cached sudo ticket before the run, refreshed in the background past sudo's 5-minute timeout; press Ctrl-D at the password prompt to skip priming (later steps then prompt for themselves as before), or Ctrl-C to abort the run entirely. A missing `sudo` binary or a declined prompt is not an error. Each run writes a per-run log under `$XDG_STATE_HOME/sysup/logs` (falling back to `~/.local/state/sysup/logs`), keeping the newest 10 files; a same-second filename collision gets a `-1`, `-2`, ... suffix. `sysup` prints the log path after every run that reaches one, clean, amber or red. A captured step's stdout/stderr lines starting with `error:` (case-insensitive) are flagged even on a zero exit code; up to 5 are printed inline, any more are summarized as `+N more, see log`. One entry producing any such lines reports a single `warned` result (amber, not red) instead of t

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from sysup.capabilities import CAPABILITIES
from sysup.capabilities.uv_tool_python import UvToolPython


class TestUvToolPython:
    @staticmethod
    def _receipt(root, tool, *, python=None, requirement=None, extra=""):
        directory = root / tool
        directory.mkdir(parents=True)
        requirement = requirement or f'["{tool}"]'
        text = f"[tool]\nrequirements = {requirement}\n"
        if python is not None:
            text += f'python = "{python}"\n'
        path = directory / "uv-receipt.toml"
        path.write_text(text + extra)
        return path

    @staticmethod
    def _fake_run(mocker, root, *, current="3.14.6\n", current_code=0, directory_code=0, directory=None, outcomes=None):
        pending = {tuple(argv): list(values) for argv, values in (outcomes or {}).items()}

        def run(argv, **kwargs):
            assert isinstance(argv, list)
            assert kwargs.get("capture_output") is True
            assert kwargs.get("text") is True
            assert kwargs.get("check") is False
            assert not kwargs.get("shell", False)
            if argv == ["/bin/mise", "current", "python"]:
                assert kwargs.get("cwd") == Path.home()
                return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, current_code, current, "")
            if argv == ["/bin/uv", "tool", "dir"]:
                return subprocess.CompletedProcess(
                    argv, directory_code, str(root) if directory is None else directory, ""
                )
            assert argv[:3] in (["/bin/uv", "python", "install"], ["/bin/uv", "tool", "install"])
            result = pending.get(tuple(argv), [(0, "")]).pop(0)
            if isinstance(result, OSError):
                raise result
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, result[0], "", result[1])

        mocker.patch("sysup.capabilities.uv_tool_python.shutil.which", side_effect=lambda name: f"/bin/{name}")
        return mocker.patch("sysup.capabilities.uv_tool_python.subprocess.run", autospec=True, side_effect=run)

    @staticmethod
    def _installs(mock_run):
        return [call.args[0] for call in mock_run.call_args_list if call.args[0][1:3] == ["tool", "install"]]

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("target", ["3.10", "3.14"])
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("structured", [False, True])
    def test_pins_unpinned_tool_to_global_minor_and_reinstalls(self, mocker, tmp_path, target, structured) -> None:
        root = tmp_path / "tools"
        requirements = '[{name = "gita", extras = [], specifier = ""}]' if structured else '["gita"]'
        first = self._receipt(root, "gita", requirement=requirements)
        second = self._receipt(root, "gita-extra")
        originals = [first.read_bytes(), second.read_bytes()]
        mock_run = self._fake_run(mocker, root, current=f"{target}.8\n")

        steps = list(UvToolPython().run())

        assert [(step.label, step.success) for step in steps] == [
            (f"gita (python unpinned -> {target})", True),
            (f"gita-extra (python unpinned -> {target})", True),
        ]
        installs = [
            ["/bin/uv", "tool", "install", "--python", target, "--force", tool] for tool in ("gita", "gita-extra")
        ]
        assert self._installs(mock_run) == installs
        calls = [call.args[0] for call in mock_run.call_args_list]
        interpreter = ["/bin/uv", "python", "install", target]
        assert calls.count(interpreter) == 1
        assert calls.index(interpreter) < calls.index(installs[0])
        assert [first.read_bytes(), second.read_bytes()] == originals

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(("old", "target"), [("3.9.9", "3.10"), ("3.13.4rc2", "3.14")])
    def test_moves_stale_pin_to_global_minor(self, mocker, tmp_path, old, target) -> None:
        root = tmp_path / "tools"
        self._receipt(root, "zulu", python=old)
        self._receipt(root, "alpha", python=old)
        self._receipt(root, "alpha-current", python=target)
        mock_run = self._fake_run(mocker, root, current=f"{target}.1\n")

        steps = list(UvToolPython().run())

        minor = ".".join(old.split(".")[:2])
        assert [(step.label, step.success) for step in steps] == [
            (f"alpha (python {minor} -> {target})", True),
            (f"zulu (python {minor} -> {target})", True),
        ]
        assert self._installs(mock_run) == [
            ["/bin/uv", "tool", "install", "--python", target, "--force", "alpha"],
            ["/bin/uv", "tool", "install", "--python", target, "--force", "zulu"],
        ]

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        ("pins", "message"),
        [
            (("3.14.1", "3.14.8rc2"), "all uv tools on python 3.14"),
            (("3.14a1", "3.14.0b2"), "all uv tools on python 3.14"),
            (("3.14", "3.15.2"), "all uv tools pinned to python 3.14 or newer"),
            (("3.15", "4.0.1"), "all uv tools pinned to python 3.14 or newer"),
        ],
    )
    def test_leaves_current_pin_untouched(self, mocker, tmp_path, pins, message) -> None:
        root = tmp_path / "tools"
        paths = [self._receipt(root, tool, python=pin) for tool, pin in zip(("gita", "beets"), pins, strict=True)]
        originals = [path.read_bytes() for path in paths]
        mock_run = self._fake_run(mocker, root)

        steps = list(UvToolPython().run())

        assert [(step.success, step.message) for step in steps] == [(True, message)]
        assert self._installs(mock_run) == []
        assert ["/bin/uv", "python", "install", "3.14"] not in [call.args[0] for call in mock_run.call_args_list]
        assert [path.read_bytes() for path in paths] == originals

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("old", [None, "3.12", "3.13"])
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("initial", [(1, "no wheel"), (1, "  "), OSError("initial spawn denied")])
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("recovery", [(0, ""), (2, "recovery denied"), OSError("rollback spawn denied")])
    def test_reverts_to_prior_interpreter_when_tool_fails_on_new_minor(
        self, mocker, tmp_path, old, initial, recovery
    ) -> None:
        root = tmp_path / "tools"
        receipt = self._receipt(root, "alpha", python=old)
        original = receipt.read_bytes()
        self._receipt(root, "zulu", python="3.11")
        target = ("/bin/uv", "tool", "install", "--python", "3.14", "--force", "alpha")
        rollback = (
            ("/bin/uv", "tool", "install", "--python", old, "--force", "alpha")
            if old
            else ("/bin/uv", "tool", "install", "--force", "alpha")
        )
        mock_run = self._fake_run(mocker, root, outcomes={target: [initial], rollback: [recovery]})

        steps = list(UvToolPython().run())

        assert [(step.label, step.success) for step in steps] == [
            (f"alpha (python {old or 'unpinned'} -> 3.14)", False),
            ("zulu (python 3.11 -> 3.14)", True),
        ]
        diagnostic = str(initial) if isinstance(initial, OSError) else initial[1].strip() or "unknown error"
        assert diagnostic in steps[0].message
        if recovery == (0, ""):
            assert (f"kept on python {old}" if old else "kept unpinned") in steps[0].message
        else:
            assert (f"reinstall on python {old} also failed" if old else "unpinned reinstall also failed") in steps[
                0

Equal and newer pins stay unchanged. Failed moves attempt rollback and report recovery failures; customized or malformed receipts are visibly skipped untouched and may still fail during later uv upgrades.
 - **dot**: `dot localize --shared <path>` opts a tracked file into a git clean/smudge filter instead of moving it: the file stays where it is, git stores the reserved `@HOME@` token in place of this host's home path, and each host's work tree gets its own home back on checkout. Combining `--shared` with `--to` is refused before any change. The filter itself is hidden plumbing git calls (`dot filter clean|smudge <path>`): a pure byte transform that preserves line endings, BOM and non-UTF-8 content, and refuses any file that already contains `@HOME@`.
 - **sysup**: a `sudo: true` flag on an entry (or any step starting with `sudo`) primes a cached sudo ticket before the run, refreshed in the background past sudo's 5-minute timeout; press Ctrl-D at the password prompt to skip priming (later steps then prompt for themselves as before), or Ctrl-C to abort the run entirely. A missing `sudo` binary or a declined prompt is not an error. Each run writes a per-run log under `$XDG_STATE_HOME/sysup/logs` (falling back to `~/.local/state/sysup/logs`), keeping the newest 10 files; a same-second filename collision gets a `-1`, `-2`, ... suffix. `sysup` prints the log path after every run that reaches one, clean, amber or red. A captured step's stdout/stderr lines starting with `error:` (case-insensitive) are flagged even on a zero exit code; up to 5 are printed inline, any more are summarized as `+N more, see log`. One entry producing any such lines reports a single `warned` result (amber, not red) instead of the usual success.

 """Phase 0: the single-instance vault lock."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from klyreon.run.lock import LockBusyError, lock_path, vault_lock

pytestmark = pytest.mark.klyreon


class TestVaultLock:
    def test_second_in_process_acquisition_is_busy(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        root = tmp_path / "vault"
        root.mkdir()
        with vault_lock(root):
            with pytest.raises(LockBusyError):
                with vault_lock(root):
                    pass

    def test_released_after_keyboard_interrupt(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        root = tmp_path / "vault"
        root.mkdir()
        with pytest.raises(KeyboardInterrupt):
            with vault_lock(root):
                raise KeyboardInterrupt
        # Lock is free again: a fresh acquisition succeeds.
        with vault_lock(root):
            pass

    def test_killed_process_leaves_no_stale_lock(self, tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
        root = tmp_path / "vault"
        root.mkdir()
        state_home = str(tmp_path / "state")
        monkeypatch.setenv("XDG_STATE_HOME", state_home)
        # A child holds the lock, then is SIGKILLed. The kernel releases the
        # flock on process death, so the parent can take it immediately after.
        src_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] / "src"
        env = dict(os.environ)
        env["XDG_STATE_HOME"] = state_home
        env["PYTHONPATH"] = os.pathsep.join([str(src_root / "tools"), str(src_root / "lib")])
        holder = (
            "import time\n"
            "from pathlib import Path\n"
            "from klyreon.run.lock import vault_lock\n"
            f"with vault_lock(Path({str(root)!r})):\n"
            "    print('locked', flush=True)\n"
            "    time.sleep(30)\n"
        )
        proc = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", holder], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, env=env)
        assert proc.stdout is not None
        line = proc.stdout.readline().strip()
        assert line == b"locked", line
        proc.kill()
        proc.wait(timeout=5)
        # No stale lock: acquisition succeeds right away.
        with vault_lock(root):
            pass

    def test_lock_path_is_stable_and_hashed(self, tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
        monkeypatch.setenv("XDG_STATE_HOME", str(tmp_path / "state"))
        root = tmp_path / "vault"
        root.mkdir()
        p1 = lock_path(root)
        p2 = lock_path(root)
        assert p1 == p2
        assert p1.suffix == ".lock"
        assert p1.name != "vault.lock"  # hashed, not the raw name


FILE src/tools/klyreon/run/lock.py 
 """Single-instance guard: two klyreon runs never touch one vault at once.

A non-blocking ``fcntl.flock`` on
``$XDG_STATE_HOME/klyreon/<sha256(root)[:12]>.lock``, held for the run and
released in ``finally`` -- so ``KeyboardInterrupt`` and every other
``BaseException`` release it, and process death releases it at the kernel level
(the claim-release invariant). This is the PRD "Single-instance guard" feature;
PRD D reuses this module.

An invocation that cannot take the lock raises :class:`LockBusyError`: the CLI
turns that into an info line and exit 0, because overlapping cron ticks are
expected, not an error.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import fcntl
import hashlib
import os
from collections.abc import Iterator
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path

__all__ = ["LockBusyError", "lock_path", "vault_lock"]


class LockBusyError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when another klyreon run already holds the vault lock."""


def _state_dir() -> Path:
    xdg = os.environ.get("XDG_STATE_HOME")
    base = Path(xdg) if xdg else Path.home() / ".local" / "state"
    return base / "klyreon"


def lock_path(root: Path) -> Path:
    """Return the lock file path for the vault at ``root``.

    The name is ``<sha256(resolved-root)[:12]>.lock`` so two vaults never share
    a lock and the name does not leak the path.
    """
    digest = hashlib.sha256(str(root.resolve()).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]
    return _state_dir() / f"{digest}.lock"


@contextmanager
def vault_lock(root: Path) -> Iterator[Path]:
    """Hold the vault lock for the duration of the ``with`` block.

    Yields the lock-file path. Releases in ``finally`` on any exit, normal or
    exceptional.

    Raises:
        LockBusyError: when another process already holds the lock.
    """
    path = lock_path(root)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # Open (not truncate) so a concurrent holder's advisory lock is what gates
    # us, never the file content. The fd is the lock's lifetime.
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o644)
    try:
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except OSError as exc:
            msg = f"another klyreon run already holds the vault lock: {path}"
            raise LockBusyError(msg) from exc
        try:
            yield path
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)

 """Settings for the ``postup`` tool."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from buvis.pybase.configuration import GlobalSettings
from pydantic_settings import SettingsConfigDict

__all__ = ["PostupSettings", "default_out_dir"]


def default_out_dir() -> Path:
    """Return the default output directory (XDG data dir).

    Returns:
        ``~/.local/share/postup`` as an absolute path.
    """
    return Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "postup"


class PostupSettings(GlobalSettings):
    """Validated ``postup`` settings.

    Layered from CLI overrides, environment variables (``BUVIS_POSTUP_``
    prefix), YAML config, and these defaults.

    Attributes:
        roots: Directories scanned for git repositories.
        excludes: Repository paths dropped from the discovered set.
        meta_repos: Claude-tooling repo roots whose sessions count as meta
            (in addition to ``~/.claude``) for the meta-budget attribution.
        out_dir: Directory the file contracts are written to.
        model: Optional Claude model name (consumed by the enrich command in a
            later PRD; carried here so the settings contract is stable).
    """

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_prefix="BUVIS_POSTUP_",
        env_nested_delimiter="__",
        case_sensitive=False,
        frozen=True,
        extra="forbid",
    )

    roots: list[str] = []
    excludes: list[str] = []
    meta_repos: list[str] = []
    out_dir: str = ""
    model: str | None = None

    @property
    def resolved_out_dir(self) -> Path:
        """Return the configured ``out_dir`` or the XDG default when unset."""
        return Path(self.out_dir).expanduser() if self.out_dir else default_out_dir()

 """Click CLI adapter for ``postup``.

The CLI layer inspects the :class:`CommandResult` and renders it through the
buvis ``console`` — command classes never print. Command classes are imported
lazily inside handlers so a bare ``postup --help`` pulls nothing heavy.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import click
from buvis.pybase.adapters import console
from buvis.pybase.configuration import buvis_options, get_settings

from postup.settings import PostupSettings

__all__ = ["cli"]


@click.group(
    help="POrtfolio STandUP — collect and render portfolio state.",
    invoke_without_command=True,
)
@buvis_options(settings_class=PostupSettings)
@click.pass_context
def cli(ctx: click.Context) -> None:
    ctx.ensure_object(dict)
    # Bare `postup` (no subcommand) runs the text brief — the default surface.
    # This path pulls in only the pure derive layer, never Textual.
    if ctx.invoked_subcommand is None:
        from postup.commands.brief.brief import CommandBrief

        settings = get_settings(ctx, PostupSettings)
        result = CommandBrief(settings).execute()
        if result.success and result.metadata.get("text"):
            console.print(str(result.metadata["text"]), mode="raw")
        console.report_result(result)


@cli.command("collect", help="Collect portfolio state into the versioned file contracts.")
@click.option("--no-fetch", is_flag=True, help="Skip 'git fetch' before reading each repo.")
@click.option("--days", type=int, default=60, show_default=True, help="Commit window in days.")
@click.pass_context
def collect(ctx: click.Context, *, no_fetch: bool, days: int) -> None:
    """Discover repos, collect their signals, and write the contracts."""
    from postup.commands.collect.collect import CommandCollect

    settings = get_settings(ctx, PostupSettings)
    result = CommandCollect(settings, fetch=not no_fetch, days=days).execute()
    console.report_result(result)


@cli.command("enrich", help="Enrich the collected data into epics.json via the claude CLI (optional).")
@click.pass_context
def enrich(ctx: click.Context) -> None:
    """Build the enrichment prompt, invoke claude, and write epics.json."""
    from postup.commands.enrich.enrich import CommandEnrich

    settings = get_settings(ctx, PostupSettings)
    result = CommandEnrich(settings).execute()
    console.report_result(result)


@cli.command("brief", help="Print the deterministic text standup from the latest data.json.")
@click.pass_context
def brief(ctx: click.Context) -> None:
    """Render the text standup (the same surface as bare ``postup``)."""
    from postup.commands.brief.brief import CommandBrief

    settings = get_settings(ctx, PostupSettings)
    result = CommandBrief(settings).execute()
    if result.success and result.metadata.get("text"):
        console.print(str(result.metadata["text"]), mode="raw")
    console.report_result(result)


@cli.command("tui", help="Open the interactive Textual standup (requires the 'postup' extra).")
@click.pass_context
def tui(ctx: click.Context) -> None:
    """Launch the Textual standup; a missing extra yields install guidance."""
    settings = get_settings(ctx, PostupSettings)
    try:
        from postup.commands.tui.tui import CommandTui
    except ImportError:
        console.require_import("postup")
        return
    result = CommandTui(settings).execute()
    console.report_result(result)


@cli.command("serve", help="Start the web dashboard (requires the 'postup-web' extra).")
@click.option("-p", "--port", default=8000, show_default=True, type=int, help="Port to listen on.")
@click.option("-H", "--host", default="127.0.0.1", show_default=True, help="Interface to bind to.")
@click.option("--no-browser", is_flag=True, default=False, help="Do not open the browser on start.")
@click.pass_context
def serve(ctx: click.Context, port: int, host: str, *, no_browser: bool) -> None:
    """Serve the portfolio web UI; a missing web extra yields install guidance."""
    from postup.commands.serve.serve import MISSING_EXTRA_ERROR, CommandServe
    from postup.params.serve import ServeParams

    settings = get_settings(ctx, PostupSettings)
    params = ServeParams(host=host, port=port, no_browser=no_browser)
    result = CommandServe(settings, params).execute()
    if not result.success and result.error == MISSING_EXTRA_ERROR:
        console.require_import("postup-web", tool_name="postup serve")
        return
    console.report_result(result)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    cli()
